On Linux everything works fine for me.  On Android however, I start to run into some interesting things.

1. When loading via ``ResourceLoader.LoadThreadedRequest(scenePath)``, it loads to 50% and then instantly switches to the other scene which is fascinating.
2. When loading via ``ResourceLoader.LoadThreadedRequest(scenePath, useSubThreads: true);`` it loads to 75% before switching on 2 of our 3 scenes.  On the 3rd scene, it hangs forever at 0%.

I have no idea if this is related, but I found the 50% thing interesting when loading linearly and the freeze with subthreads.  I will have to put together a separate mrp so you guys can test.  In summary:

```
ResourceLoader.LoadThreadedRequest(scenePath)
```

10% -> 23% -> 35% -> 50% -> switch scene

```
ResourceLoader.LoadThreadedRequest(scenePath, useSubThreads: true);
```

0% -> 75% -> switch scene

on all except 1 which hangs.

Tbh, the first one likely isn't an issue.  Its hard to know which assets will take longer to load than others, so a clean 0% -> 100% is hard to achieve.  But the hang is definitely a bug.

After pulling my hair out why `LoadThreadedGetStatus` was returning InvalidResource (after requesting it properly), even though the scene works just fine separately and with `ResourceLoader.Load<PackedScene>`, I stumbled upon these issues here. As of now (4.4.1.stable.mono) this feature seems completely useless. If someone could figure out why this is happening and a fix, it would be greatly appreciated ❤

I believe I just stumbled upon what I believe is same issue as this. In my case I am running a bigger chunk of code in a separate thread, in which I load and instantiate many packedScenes, either through direct Exports or through ResourceLoader.LoadThreadedRequest, before adding them all back to the scene tree through a deferred call. Randomly, when this thread runs, other operations that are happening in the main thread end up deadlocked, which effectively makes my whole game freeze

The line where the freeze actually occurs is random but consistent. When I press play, it will always freeze at the at the same line of my code. If I make a change completely unrelated to that line, however, such as commenting out a method call somewhere else, the freeze will be caused by a completely different line of code, if it will happen at all. By debugging, I see that I am always getting stuck at the _scriptTypeBiMap.ReadWriteLock of the ScriptManagerBridge class

I have experimented replacing every ResourceLoader.LoadThreadedRequest call by ResourceLoader.Load both in main thread code and in my separate thread. This caused the freezing to stop, but given the random nature of the issue I have a hard time saying that this solved it since I am still loading resources from a separate thread anyway, and that is bound to pass through that same ReedWriteLock that is causing the deadlocks

I have given this issue some more thought and I have a theory on how to fix it, but unfortunately I'm not equipped to compile and test godot

From what I understand, as described on #99798, the source of this issue is the fact that, while loading a script and while the lock is acquired, dependencies might have to be loaded as well. If the loading is made from a worker thread, a new thread will be created and go through the same lock, and therefore the deadlock will happen as the previous thread already had locked it. Debugging on VS, this is exactly what I saw, it tries to load a class while loading a resource through `ResourceLoader.LoadThreadedRequest`, and then tries to load it's base class, which it fails to due to the lock

The fix proposal above was to remove the `godot_sharp_internal_script_load` from the lock, which might have fixed the issue, but instead it was preferred to go with #99539, which keeps that call in the lock, but instead used an actual ReadWrite lock so that, in theory, the deadlock couldn't happen anymore

The issue, however, is that the actual behavior of the lock remained exactly the same! All lock calls were replaced by `ReaderWriterLockSlim.EnterUpgradeableReadLock` and additional `ReaderWriterLockSlim.EnterWriteLock` calls were added. An UpgradeableReadLock can run in parallel with other ReadLocks, but not with other UpgradeableReadLocks, so despite all the apparent Read locking, there is never more than one thread reading at the same time. When `godot_sharp_internal_script_load` is called the thread is not under a write lock, but it is under an upgradeable lock, and so the new thread to load any dependencies gets stuck

Considering all that, my proposal would be to mix both solutions, keeping `godot_sharp_internal_script_load` inside a read lock but not in a upgradeable lock. According to the [ReaderWriterLockSlim documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/fundamentals/runtime-libraries/system-threading-readerwriterlockslim#upgrade-and-downgrade-locks), it is possible to downgrade a lock back to a normal ReadLock simply by calling `ReaderWriterLockSlim.EnterReadLock`. Releasing the lock is still be done with `ReaderWriterLockSlim.ExitUpgradeableReadLock` so `ReaderWriterLockSlim.ExitReadLock` is not required

I do not have enough knowledge of the `ScriptManagerBridge` class to know just where Read locks actually need to be upgradeable or not, but I am under the impression that `godot_sharp_internal_script_load` could be done in a Read only lock by downgrading it. Right after it, the code my either call `GetOrCreateScriptBridgeForType` or `AddScriptBridgeCore`, but each of these start by already acquiring a lock, so I'm led to believe that there won't be a problem if another Upgradeable lock is acquired before those methods are actually executed. If this is a problem, then we might need to rethink if loading dependencies should actually create a new thread or not

I hope these findings help shed some light on how to fix this issue :)

@dougVanny Oh, if there's a section not needing an upgradeable lock, a plain read one makes sense indeed. As it does any combination of locks/upgrades/downgrades that keeps the original intent. Also, it may be the case that in some sections it's not necessary to have a read lock upgraded to write, being possible instead to read-lock, unlock and finally write-lock. However, I didn't want to break the critical section because I couldn't be sure I wouldn't be introducing any race conditions by doing so.
